intended_object: A bundle of the numerical data, with its exact values, used in the free-beam worked example of Section 9 of Davis–Kahan (1970): the range of ε, a lower bound on the third eigenvalue, the residual Gram matrices and the Ritz values. Inferred from the docstring ("finite-data package", "theorem boundary").
explanation: The docstring calls this structure a "theorem boundary". It is a record that any concrete analytic model of the paper's free-beam example has to supply. It collects the hypotheses 0 < ε < 100 and 500 < (third eigenvalue), plus several fields, each paired with a proof that it equals an explicit closed-form quantity defined earlier in the same file (residualGram ε, ritzLow ε, ritzHigh ε, orthogonalResidualGram ε). So it is a bookkeeping device for organising one example's proof. The literature has no mathematical object that this structure is meant to define, so it cannot be judged faithful or unfaithful to one.
